gloss: apprentice; disciple; pupil in a trade

definitions.gloss: apprentice; disciple; pupil learning a trade or craft
definitions.explanation: A person learning a trade, craft, or art under the guidance of a master. Implies a traditional master-apprentice relationship where skills are passed down through hands-on training.

examples.japanese: {徒弟|とてい}⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}ぶ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
examples.english: To learn skills through an apprenticeship system.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}、⟦{大工|だいく}→大工：04051_daiku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{徒弟|とてい}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{働|はたら}いていた→働く：00503_hataraku⟧。
examples.english: When he was young, he worked as a carpenter's apprentice.

examples.japanese: ⟦かつて→かつて：10303_katsute⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{職人|しょくにん}→職人：09868_shokunin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{世界|せかい}→世界：01447_sekai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{徒弟|とてい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{何年|なんねん}→何年：12737_nannen⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦かけて→かける：00854_kakeru⟧{親方|おやかた}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{技|わざ}→技：02172_waza⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{盗|ぬす}む→盗む：01166_nusumu⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}えた→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧ものだ。
examples.english: In the old world of craftsmen, apprentices would spend years learning the master's skills by watching and imitating.

notes:
A compound of {徒|と} (follower, companion) and {弟|てい} (younger person, disciple). A somewhat formal or literary word that evokes the traditional system of learning trades through direct apprenticeship under a master ({親方|おやかた} or ⟦{師匠|ししょう}→師匠：12421_shishou⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {徒弟|とてい}⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧: apprenticeship system
- {徒弟|とてい}⟦{教育|きょういく}→教育：01313_kyouiku⟧: apprentice training
- {徒弟|とてい}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧: to work as an apprentice
- {徒弟|とてい}⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧: master-apprentice relationship

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{弟子|でし}→弟子：03986_deshi⟧: disciple, pupil — more general and common; used for martial arts, traditional arts, and academic mentorship
- ⟦{見習|みなら}い→見習い：18735_minarai⟧: trainee, intern — modern term for someone learning on the job
- {丁稚|でっち}: shop boy, young apprentice — historical term for child apprentices in merchant houses

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {徒弟|とてい}⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧ was the primary way trades were transmitted in pre-modern Japan. While formal apprenticeship has declined, its spirit survives in fields like ⟦{寿司|すし}→寿司：04946_sushi⟧ making, ⟦{落語|らくご}→落語：04457_rakugo⟧, and traditional crafts, where years of training under a master are still expected.
